gloss: food, clothing, and shelter; basic necessities of life

definitions.gloss: food, clothing, and shelter; the three basic necessities of life
definitions.explanation: A set phrase referring to the fundamental requirements for human living. Composed of 衣 (clothing) + 食 (food) + 住 (housing). Often used when discussing standards of living or basic needs.

examples.japanese: {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}に{困|こま}らない{生活|せいかつ}がしたい。
examples.english: I want a life where I don't have to worry about the basics.

examples.japanese: {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}が{整|ととの}って{初|はじ}めて、{人|ひと}は{安心|あんしん}できる。
examples.english: People can feel at ease only when their basic needs are met.

examples.japanese: {留学|りゅうがく}{先|さき}では{衣食住|いしょくじゅう}すべてを{自分|じぶん}で{管理|かんり}しなければならなかった。
examples.english: While studying abroad, I had to manage all my basic living needs by myself.

notes:
USAGE:
{衣食住|いしょくじゅう} is a concise expression for the three pillars of daily life. It is commonly used in discussions about living standards, budgeting, and social welfare.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}に{困|こま}る (to struggle with basic needs)
- {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}が{足|た}りる (to have enough for basic needs)
- {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}を{整|ととの}える (to get one's basic needs in order)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Japanese order (clothing, food, housing) differs from the typical English order (food, clothing, shelter). The expression {衣食住|いしょくじゅう}{足|た}りて{礼節|れいせつ}を{知|し}る (when one has enough to eat and wear, one learns manners) is a well-known proverb.
